name: Arlo
waitingLines: Small thing, but I’d really like to say hi to {partner} before I go. Cracker?
Small thing, but I saved {partner} the best cracker. I’m guarding it till they’re back.

questions.scene: Arlo shuffles in, sniffing your floorboards like they owe him money.
lines: Small thing, but I brought a quiz. And crackers. Mostly crackers. Okay, question!
questions.question: What does the name 'aardvark' mean?

choices.label: Ant vacuum
reply: Honestly accurate. Not the answer though.
It means 'earth pig,' from Afrikaans.
We're not pigs. We're just enthusiastic about dirt.

choices.label: Earth pig
reply: Yes! Earth pig. Pia calls me that when I hog the blanket.
It comes from Afrikaans: 'aarde' means earth, 'vark' means pig.
Not a pig, by the way. Just digs like one. Eats like one too.

choices.label: Snout king
reply: I'll take it as a compliment! But no.
It means 'earth pig' in Afrikaans.
Pia says snout king is my royal title now. No take-backs.

questions.scene: Arlo holds up a red coffee cherry from a plant, squinting.
lines: Small thing, but this is where coffee comes from. I didn't know.
questions.question: What are coffee beans, actually?

choices.label: The seeds inside a cherry-like fruit
reply: Yes! Coffee beans are seeds!
They grow inside red 'coffee cherries,' usually two per fruit.
Pia's morning mood depends on a fruit seed. Respect the seed.

choices.label: Beans from a bean plant, like green beans
reply: Nope! Not related to green beans!
They're seeds inside a red, cherry-like fruit.
The fruit is edible too. Sweet, even.

choices.label: Tree roots
reply: Ha! No!
Coffee beans are seeds inside a red coffee cherry.
Pia would be very upset if coffee were roots.

questions.factBasis: Coffee beans are seeds of the coffee cherry (Coffea fruit).

questions.scene: Arlo picks up a building block from your shelf and studies it.
lines: This one is weird. Very weird.
questions.question: Which animal makes cube-shaped poop?

choices.label: Penguin
reply: Penguins are elegant! No cubes!
It's the wombat. Their poop comes out cube-shaped.
Their intestines have stretchy and stiff sections that form the corners.

choices.label: Giraffe
reply: Ha! Imagine dropping that from that height.
It's the wombat! Cubes!
They use the cubes to mark territory, and cubes don't roll away. Genius.

choices.label: Wombat
reply: YES. Wombat cubes! Nature's dice!
Their intestines shape it into cubes as it dries.
They stack them to mark territory. Pia wants me to stop telling this at dinner.

questions.scene: Arlo boops your nose with his paw, then looks at the paw.
lines: Small thing, but dogs have a special ID system. Right there on their nose.
questions.question: What's unique about a dog's nose print?

choices.label: It changes color with the weather
reply: Ha! Mood nose! No!
Every dog's nose print has a unique pattern.
Like fingerprints, but cuter and wetter.

choices.label: Its pattern is unique, like a fingerprint
reply: Yes! Unique nose prints!
Each dog's nose has its own pattern of ridges and bumps.
Some places even use them for identification. Boop ID.

choices.label: All dogs have the same nose print
reply: Nope! Every dog's is different!
Nose prints are unique, like fingerprints.
Boop with confidence. Each boop is unique.

questions.factBasis: Dog nose prints have unique ridge patterns, comparable to fingerprints.

questions.scene: Arlo puts his ear to the ground, eyes wide.
lines: Small thing, but this happens only every 13 or 17 years.
questions.question: What do periodical cicadas do between their emergences?

choices.label: Migrate south for the winter
reply: No flying south! They stay put. Underground.
Periodical cicadas spend 13 or 17 years underground feeding on root sap.
Then they all come up at once. Huge, loud party.

choices.label: Live underground, sipping tree roots, for 13 or 17 years
reply: Yes! Long underground lives!
They drink sap from tree roots, then emerge all at once.
Billions sometimes. It's like a surprise party that took 17 years to plan.

choices.label: Sleep in tree branches
reply: Nope, they're underground the whole time!
13 or 17 years below ground, sipping root sap.
Then they all pop up at once and sing their hearts out.

questions.factBasis: Periodical cicadas live underground 13 or 17 years feeding on xylem from roots.

questions.scene: Arlo sticks his tongue out, very far, then quickly pulls it back in. Embarrassed.
lines: Don't be weird about this.
questions.question: About how long can an aardvark's tongue get?

choices.label: About 12 inches
reply: Yep! Basically a ruler!
Around 30 centimeters, long and sticky for scooping termites.
Pia once asked me to grab the remote with it. I did. We don't talk about it.

choices.label: About 2 inches
reply: Ha! Cute. Way longer.
Aardvark tongues can reach around 12 inches.
Perfect for slurping termites. Terrible for kissing. Pia disagrees.

choices.label: About 6 feet
reply: Okay, that's a garden hose, not a tongue!
It's around 12 inches. Still very long!
Long enough to slurp tens of thousands of termites in a night.

questions.scene: Arlo eats bamboo-flavored crackers very slowly, one after another.
lines: Small thing, but pandas would beat me in a snack contest.
questions.question: About how many hours a day can giant pandas spend eating?

choices.label: About 1 hour
reply: Way more! Way, way more!
Pandas can eat 10 to 16 hours a day.
Bamboo isn't very nutritious, so they eat constantly.

choices.label: They don't eat at all
reply: A panda on a diet? Never!
They eat 10 to 16 hours a day.
Bamboo all day. The ultimate snack schedule.

choices.label: About 10 to 16 hours
reply: Yes! Most of the day!
Bamboo has few nutrients, so pandas eat a LOT of it.
They're basically professional snackers. Goals.

questions.factBasis: Giant pandas spend roughly 10–16 hours a day feeding.

questions.scene: Arlo spots a photo of two prairie dogs touching faces on your wall.
lines: This is the cutest greeting ever.
questions.question: How do prairie dogs greet family members?

choices.label: They high-five
reply: Ha! Love it. Not it.
They touch teeth and noses, like a little kiss.
It helps them recognize their own family members.

choices.label: They ignore each other
reply: Nope! Super social!
They greet with a 'kiss,' touching teeth.
Family recognition. Very wholesome.

choices.label: They touch teeth, like a little kiss
reply: Yes! A prairie dog kiss!
They press their mouths together to recognize family.
Pia and I tried. It was mostly nose. Still cute.

questions.factBasis: Prairie dogs greet relatives with 'greet kisses' (touching teeth).

questions.scene: Arlo fans himself with a paper plate.
lines: Termites are smarter than my thermostat.
questions.question: How do some termite mounds stay cool in hot weather?

choices.label: The termites flap their wings constantly
reply: Ha! Exhausting! No.
The mound's tunnels and chimneys move air around.
Natural ventilation. Engineers took notes.

choices.label: Tunnels and chimneys move air through the mound
reply: Yes! Natural air conditioning!
Air flows through chimneys and tunnels, helping keep the nest comfortable.
Architects have even copied the idea for buildings. Termites: honored.

choices.label: They put ice in the middle
reply: Where would they get ice?!
The mound is built with air channels that help control temperature.
It's basically a breathing building.

questions.factBasis: Termite mounds use passive ventilation; inspired Eastgate Centre design.

questions.scene: Arlo grabs your hand, then lets go, very shy.
lines: Small thing, but this is the cutest fact ever.
questions.question: What do sea otters sometimes do while they sleep?

choices.label: Hold hands so they don't drift apart
reply: YES. I'm crying. They hold hands.
Sea otters often hold paws or wrap in kelp so they don't float away.
Pia and I tried it. Our burrow doesn't have currents. Still nice.

choices.label: Sleep on the beach in a pile
reply: Nope! They sleep in the water.
They hold paws so they don't drift apart.
Sometimes they wrap themselves in kelp too. Ocean blankets.

choices.label: Snore really loudly
reply: Maybe! But that's not the fact.
Sea otters hold hands so they don't drift apart.
Love that keeps you anchored. Literally.

questions.factBasis: Sea otters sometimes hold paws or wrap in kelp while resting.

questions.scene: Arlo eyes your toothbrush cup with deep suspicion.
lines: This matters to me. A lot.
questions.question: Toothpaste: squeeze from the middle, from the end, or roll it up?

choices.label: From the middle
reply: A middle squeezer! No judgment.
Okay, a tiny bit of judgment. Pia does it too.

choices.label: From the end
reply: From the end. Neat and tidy, I respect it.
The tube is calm. The tube feels safe.

choices.label: Roll it up
reply: Rolled up?! You're an artist.
Pia would like to meet you. Professionally.

A:A: So you and {partner} are both middle squeezers! That's lovely.
No tube wars in your house. Just chaos, shared equally.
Honestly, that's what love is.
A:B: Neat and tidy from the end. I respect it.
But {partner} might still squeeze from the middle. Don't fight, okay?
Think of their messy tube as a love note. A squished one.
A:C: {partner} squeezes from the middle. An artist and a rebel!
Be gentle when you fix it every morning. It's love maintenance.
B:A: A middle squeezer, no judgment.
But {partner} squeezes from the end. Tiny tube war ahead.
Buy two tubes. Trust me. It saved my relationship.
B:B: You both squeeze from the end! A tidy household.
The tube in your bathroom is living its best life with {partner}.
Pia and I could never. We've tried. Twice.
B:C: You roll it up. {partner} squeezes from the end.
Two tidy approaches. That's a strong team.
Just don't swap tubes by accident. It'll confuse everyone.
C:A: But {partner} rolls it up like a pro.
Let them fix the tube. You bring the snacks. Fair trade.
C:B: {partner} rolls it up. You're both tidy people. Rare!
Different technique, same energy. Tube-approved couple.
C:C: You both roll it up! Gallery-worthy bathroom.
Honestly, {partner} and you probably fold towels into swans too.
Pia and I are officially jealous. Teach us.

questions.scene: Arlo notices your window cracked open and sniffs the breeze.
lines: Pia and I fight about this every single night.
questions.question: Bedroom window at night: open a crack, or sealed shut?

choices.label: Open a crack
reply: Brave! Fresh air and a cold nose.
Pia would sleep with the window open in a snowstorm.

choices.label: Sealed shut
reply: Cozy fortress mode. Respect.
A sealed burrow is a happy burrow.

A:A: You both sleep with a crack open! Matching cold noses.
Nobody negotiates the window in your house. {partner} and you just agree.
Must be nice. Pia and I have a treaty.
A:B: Sealed shut for you. Cozy fortress.
But {partner} wants fresh air. Classic Pia-and-me energy.
Half-open window, extra blanket for you. Done. You're welcome.
B:A: A crack of fresh air for you. Brave!
But {partner} wants it sealed shut. Cold nose versus warm blanket.
Try a tiny crack and an extra blanket on their side. Peace achieved.
B:B: You both like it sealed shut! A warm little fortress.
I can picture it: {partner} and you sleep like toasty burritos. No drafts allowed.
Sweet dreams, you two. Very jealous.

questions.scene: Arlo looks at your couch, then out the window, torn.
lines: Small thing, but this is a big decision.
questions.question: Perfect lazy day: stay in all day, or a picnic outside?

choices.label: Stay in all day
reply: Blanket fort life. I'm already there.
Snacks within arm's reach. No shoes required.

choices.label: Picnic outside
reply: Fresh air and cracker crumbs!
Ants as guests. They'll bring friends.

A:A: Stay-in day for both of you! Blankets, snacks, zero plans.
{partner} and you don't leave the couch. That's an order.
Honestly the best kind of date.
A:B: Picnic for you. Yay sunshine!
But {partner} wants to stay in the blanket fort. Classic.
Take the blanket outside and nap in the sun. Both win.
B:A: Stay in for you. Blanket fort time.
But {partner} wants a picnic. Hmm.
Picnic in the living room. Crumbs included. Everyone's happy.
B:B: Picnic for both of you! Fresh air date locked in.
Lowkey, you and {partner} probably have a picnic blanket ready by the door.
Pack crackers. Pack extra crackers. Ants are coming.

questions.scene: Arlo spots a sticky note on your fridge and smiles knowingly.
lines: Apologies are my specialty. I do a lot of them.
questions.question: After a small fight, what feels best?

choices.label: A note
reply: A note! Soft and sweet.
Written words can hug too.

choices.label: Saying it out loud
reply: Out loud. Brave. Face to face.
Hard to say, easy to feel.

choices.label: A snack first, words after
reply: The snack rule! Genius.
A crunch before a big feeling.

A:A: You both pick notes! Tiny letter exchange.
{partner} and you probably have a drawer full of 'sorry' notes.
Keep them. Read them on anniversaries. Cry a little.
A:B: Out loud for you. Brave!
But {partner} would rather get a note.
Say it, then leave a sticky note on their pillow. Double sorry.
A:C: Tuck the note under the snack plate. Crunch and read.
B:A: A note for you. Soft and sweet.
But {partner} needs to hear it out loud.
Write it, then read it to them. Both love languages covered.
B:B: You both say it out loud! Brave couple.
So you and {partner} just look each other in the eye and fix it.
That's rare. Pia and I need snacks first.
B:C: A snack first for you. Smart.
{partner} wants to hear it out loud.
Snack, then talk. The full apology combo. Patent pending.
C:A: Tape the note to a cookie. Perfect delivery system.
C:B: Out loud for you. So brave.
{partner} wants a snack first. Honestly, snacks make words easier.
Bring a cracker. Then speak. Trust the process.
C:C: Snack first, words after! You two follow the Arlo Rule.
Honestly, {partner} and you probably have a designated 'sorry snack.'
Pia and I are so proud of you.

questions.scene: Arlo peeks into your kitchen, humming off-key.
lines: Kitchens are where relationships are tested.
questions.question: Dinner at home: cook together, or one cooks and one cleans?

choices.label: Cook together
reply: Elbows and spoons! Chaos with kisses.
The soup might be bad. The night will be great.

choices.label: One cooks, one cleans
reply: A well-oiled machine!
Efficient and secretly romantic.

A:A: You both want to cook together! Elbows, spoons, chaos.
Every dinner with {partner} is a date. Soup optional.
Pia and I tried. The smoke alarm joined us.
A:B: One cooks, one cleans for you. Efficient.
But {partner} wants to cook side by side.
Let them stir the soup while you set the table. Close enough.
B:A: Cook together for you. So cute.
But {partner} likes one cooks, one cleans.
Cook together, then split the dishes. Or bribe them with dessert.
B:B: You both like split duty. Well-oiled team.
I can picture it: {partner} and you never argue about who does what. Efficient love.
Somebody give you two a trophy.

questions.scene: Arlo finds a party hat on your shelf and puts it on, very seriously.
lines: Small thing, but this could go very wrong.
questions.question: If you threw your partner a surprise party, how would they react?
questions.selfQuestion: If your partner threw you a surprise party, how would you react?

choices.label: Love it
reply: A party lover! Confetti everywhere.
They'll be glowing all night.

choices.label: Hate it
reply: Yikes, a quiet soul.
A surprise party is a gamble. Noted.

choices.label: Pretend to love it
reply: The polite smile! I know it well.
Smiles outside, panic inside.

A:A: You'd love it, and {partner} called it!
They know you well. Start planning the confetti.
Pia threw me one. I cried. Happy tears.
A:B: You'd hate it, but {partner} guessed you'd love it. Yikes!
There might be a surprise party in your future.
Tell them now. Before the balloons arrive.
A:C: You'd pretend. But {partner} guessed you'd love it.
Your polite smile is very convincing. Too convincing.
Maybe tell them the truth gently. Over snacks.
B:A: You'd love it! But {partner} guessed you'd hate it.
They've been protecting you from parties for no reason.
Tell them you love surprises. Prepare for confetti.
B:B: You'd hate it, and {partner} knew!
They read you perfectly. No parties, ever.
Surprise quiet dinner instead. Much safer.
B:C: You'd pretend. But {partner} guessed you'd hate it.
They suspect more than you think.
Close enough. They'll probably plan something small.
C:A: You'd love it, but {partner} thought you'd just pretend.
Your real joy looked fake to them. Oops!
Tell them it's real. Then let them plan one.
C:B: You'd hate it. {partner} thought you'd pretend. So close!
They know you'd be polite. They just don't know how much you'd suffer.
Be honest. They'll plan a quiet dinner instead.
C:C: You'd pretend to love it, and {partner} guessed it! Busted.
They see right through your polite smile.
That's real love. Seeing through the smile.

questions.scene: Arlo sniffs a glowing mushroom by your door, eyes wide.
lines: This is a personality test.
questions.question: Your partner finds a pretty glowing mushroom. What do they do?
questions.selfQuestion: You find a pretty glowing mushroom. What do you do?

choices.label: Bring it home to share
reply: A romantic! Glowing gifts are the best gifts.
Pia would cry.

choices.label: Tuck it away as a secret treasure
reply: A collector! They have plans.
A secret mushroom museum is coming.

A:A: You'd bring it home to share, and {partner} knew!
They know you share every shiny thing you find.
Glowing gifts for everyone.
A:B: You'd keep it as a treasure. {partner} guessed you'd share.
They're waiting for a glowing gift. It's in your drawer.
Let them admire it. Just for a minute. Then hide it again.
B:A: You'd bring it home to share. {partner} guessed you'd keep it.
They think you're a secret collector. You're a sharer!
Surprise them tonight with the glow.
B:B: You'd keep it as a treasure, and {partner} called it!
They know about the secret collection. They've seen the drawer.
The mushroom museum is officially open.

questions.scene: Arlo notices a blanket draped over your couch and nods slowly.
lines: Rough days happen. Pia had one yesterday. I brought crackers. It helped. Mostly.
questions.question: After a rough day, what does your partner want?
questions.selfQuestion: After a rough day, what do you want?

choices.label: Space and quiet
reply: Quiet mode. Understood.
Sometimes a closed door is a hug.

choices.label: A big hug
reply: A hugger! Arms ready.
Hugs fix half of everything.

choices.label: A snack and a rant
reply: Snack and rant combo. Classic.
Bring the good crackers.

A:A: You want quiet, and {partner} knew!
That's real attention. They give you space before you ask.
Gold star for {partner}. Quiet gold star.
A:B: You want a hug. {partner} guessed space.
They're giving you room when you want arms.
Ask for the hug out loud. They'll be so relieved.
A:C: You want a snack and a rant. {partner} guessed space.
They're tiptoeing away. You're holding crackers and complaints.
Call them back. Hand them a cracker. Start ranting.
B:A: You want quiet. {partner} guessed a hug.
They're coming in with open arms. You need ten minutes alone.
Tell them: quiet first, hug later. A delayed hug still counts.
B:B: You want a big hug, and {partner} knew it!
Their arms were already open before you walked in.
That's the dream, honestly.
B:C: You want a snack and a rant. {partner} guessed a hug.
They want to hold you. You want to vent.
Rant into the hug. Best of both.
C:A: You want quiet. {partner} guessed a snack and a rant.
They're ready to listen. You're ready to be silent.
Say 'quiet first, snacks later.' They'll get it.
C:B: You want a hug. {partner} guessed a snack and rant.
Close! Just add a hug to the snack.
C:C: You want a snack and a rant, and {partner} guessed it!
They'll bring the crackers and nod at every complaint.
Pia and I do this every Tuesday.

questions.scene: Arlo eyes a single cookie on your counter. He doesn't move. Neither do you.
lines: Small thing, but this one's life or death.
questions.question: One cookie left. What would your partner do?
questions.selfQuestion: One cookie left. What would you do?

choices.label: Offer it to the other one
reply: Aww, a generous soul.
I'd cry at the cookie.

choices.label: Eat it immediately
reply: Ruthless! A real cookie monster.
No regrets. Delicious.

A:A: You'd offer it, and {partner} knew it!
They know you'd give away the last cookie every time.
Bake two next time. Everyone gets one.
A:B: You'd eat it immediately. {partner} thought you'd share.
They believed in your generosity. Oops.
Next time, break it in half. Rebuild their trust.
B:A: You'd offer it. {partner} thought you'd eat it immediately.
They underestimated your sweetness.
Hand it over. Watch them melt. Like the chocolate chips.
B:B: You'd eat it immediately, and {partner} knew!
They've watched you inhale it before. No hesitation.
Respect. Cookies wait for no one.

questions.scene: Arlo yawns very loudly, then looks at you like he's sorry.
lines: Sleep habits say everything. Everything.
questions.question: How does your partner fall asleep?

choices.label: Instantly, mid-sentence
reply: Instantly! A sleep champion.
One second awake, next second gone.

choices.label: After scrolling for an hour
reply: Scrolling for an hour. Relatable.
Just one more video. Then twelve more.

A:A: Instant sleeper, and {partner} knew!
They've watched you fall asleep mid-sentence. Many times.
Pia says I do it mid-word. Very efficient.
A:B: You scroll for an hour. {partner} thought you'd sleep instantly.
They're asleep. You're watching cooking videos.
Put the phone down. Or send them one in the morning.
B:A: You fall asleep instantly. {partner} thought you'd scroll.
They didn't realize you're gone the second your head hits the pillow.
Lucky you. Maybe teach them the trick.
B:B: Scrolling for an hour, and {partner} knew!
They've seen the glow of your phone at 1 a.m.
Respect. Just one more video, right?
